examples.solution_text:
The known angle is between the two sides used in the area formula.
$\begin{aligned} A&=\frac12 ab\sin C\\84&=\frac12(12)x\sin100^{\circ}\\x&=\frac{84}{6\sin100^{\circ}}\\&\approx14.22\text{ cm}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned} A&=\frac12 ab\sin\theta\\43.2&=\frac12(9)(16)\sin\theta\\\sin\theta&=\frac{43.2}{72}\\&=0.6\\\theta&=\sin^{-1}(0.6)\\&\approx36.8699^{\circ}\end{aligned}$
The angle is acute, so use the inverse-sine result.
$\begin{aligned} \text{Minutes}&=0.8699\ldots\times60\\&\approx52\\\theta&\approx36^{\circ}52'\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned} A&=\frac12 ab\sin\theta\\18&=\frac12(6)(10)\sin\theta\\\sin\theta&=\frac{18}{30}\\&=0.6\end{aligned}$
Inverse sine gives the acute angle. The required obtuse angle is its supplement.
$\begin{aligned} \theta&=180^{\circ}-\sin^{-1}(0.6)\\&\approx143.1^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

Both sides forming the apex angle have length $x$.
$\begin{aligned} A&=\frac12 x^{2}\sin60^{\circ}\\16\sqrt3&=\frac12 x^{2}\left(\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\right)\\16\sqrt3&=\frac{\sqrt3}{4}x^{2}\\x^{2}&=64\\x&=\sqrt{64}\\&=8\text{ cm}\end{aligned}$
Use the positive square root because $x$ is a length.

First find the angle between the equal sides.
$\begin{aligned} C&=180^{\circ}-2(65^{\circ})\\&=50^{\circ}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned} A&=\frac12 x^{2}\sin C\\45&=\frac12 x^{2}\sin50^{\circ}\\x^{2}&=\frac{90}{\sin50^{\circ}}\\x&=\sqrt{\frac{90}{\sin50^{\circ}}}\\&\approx10.84\text{ cm}\end{aligned}$

coverage.summary: Authored five worked examples covering every distinct assessed method, including nearest-minute angles, obtuse-angle selection, exact equal-side lengths and deriving the apex angle. Questions and solutions are separate editable fields. Diagrams use black ink and declared 10 pt labels; solution prose and mathematics inherit the renderer's blue. Practice and quiz mathematics were neither changed nor re-audited. Actual rendering and final-size visual verification remain for the capture stage.

examples.derivation: 84 = (1/2)(12)x sin(100°), so x = 14/sin(100°) = 14.2159725664… cm, rounding to 14.22 cm. The marked angle lies between the known and unknown sides.
sin(theta) = 2(43.2)/(9 × 16) = 0.6. The acute angle is 36.8698976458…°. Its fractional degrees give 52.1938587506… minutes, so theta = 36°52′ to the nearest minute.
sin(theta) = 2(18)/(6 × 10) = 0.6. The obtuse solution is 180° − arcsin(0.6) = 143.1301023542…°, rounding to 143.1°. Supplement selection follows the supplied accepted theory.
16√3 = (1/2)x² sin(60°) = (√3/4)x². Therefore x² = 64 and the positive length is exactly 8 cm. Both equal sides form the marked apex angle.
The apex angle is 180° − 2(65°) = 50°. Then 45 = (1/2)x² sin(50°), giving x = √(90/sin(50°)) = 10.8391261659… cm, rounding to 10.84 cm.
